Inputs: area index $A2; concatenated $FF-terminated source lists beginning at $94BF; line/slope parameters consumed by the compiler and Multiply
Outputs: emits endpoint, gradient, flags, and optional-action fields as six-byte records beginning at $F7EA and writes a zero terminator at the next record
Assumptions: $A2 identifies an existing terminated list and enough RAM is available from $F7EA upward
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and collision-compiler arithmetic/pointer scratch
Hardware changes: none; writes RAM beneath the KERNAL region under the game's all-RAM banking model

Purpose: compute an unsigned 8-by-8-bit product for collision arithmetic
Inputs: X = unsigned multiplicand; Y = unsigned multiplier
Outputs: Y:X = 16-bit unsigned product
Assumptions: ordinary NMOS 6502 shift/add arithmetic and scratch $45-$47 are available
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $45-$47
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: test the candidate movement segment against every compiled collision record and report collision plus any encoded trigger
Inputs: X = heading/direction selector; old and candidate coordinates $48-$4B; movement profile $027F; six-byte records beginning at $F7EA
Outputs: returns A=$FF for collision or A=0 for none and restores X from $F3; records the matched record offset in $24; an eligible special segment may set action $80 and OR trigger/collision state into $81
Assumptions: the compiled table is zero-terminated and each nonzero record has the verified six-byte layout
Clobbers: A, Y, flags and collision arithmetic scratch including $23/$24,$45-$47,$F3; X is restored on return
Hardware changes: none

Purpose: invoke sprite composition in the requested masked or collision mode. Inputs: A is mode plus the named compositor's normal actor and frame context. Outputs: composite sprite buffers and metadata are produced. Assumptions: the shared compositor inputs are valid. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and extensive compositor scratch. Purpose: decode one actor frame descriptor into positioned logical sprite components, temporarily exposing RAM beneath KERNAL for high-memory source data
Inputs: A = frame attribute/modifier; Y = frame-descriptor index; X = first logical-sprite slot; actor state including $70,$72,$7D and frame pointer tables at $BC8B
Outputs: writes component bitmap references, positions, flags, and ready state into logical sprite arrays $0200-$0258 and sets sprite-dirty state as required
Assumptions: frame pointers/descriptors are valid and the caller enters with the normal $01 banking value expected by the matching INC restoration
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and sprite-composition scratch including $F1,$92,$9F
Hardware changes: decrements then restores CPU port $01 to expose high RAM transiently; does not directly write VIC-II sprite registers

Purpose: Enter The Basement playable phase's common sprite-composition body with the mode already prepared by the masked-mode caller.
Inputs: A/$F1 and $92 contain the prepared composition mode; X selects the logical sprite group; Y selects the frame descriptor; CPU port $01 is in the engine's normal I/O-visible state.
Outputs: Decrements $01 for the required high-memory RAM visibility, resolves and composes the selected frame into logical sprite work buffers, restores $01 before return, and records composition state.
Assumptions: The frame descriptor and phase sprite tables are valid; the routine's balanced DEC/INC of $01 is not interrupted by an alternate exit.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02/$03, $92/$97/$9F, $F1, and logical sprite work buffers.
Hardware changes: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently by one decrement and a balancing increment to expose the required high-memory RAM; writes sprite work buffers, not VIC-II registers directly.

Purpose: Finish The Basement playable phase's empty composite-sprite slot by marking its descriptor and restoring CPU-port banking.
Inputs: X selects the logical sprite descriptor at $0218,X; the caller entered with $01 decremented for RAM-under-KERNAL access.
Outputs: Sets bit 6 in $0218,X, increments $01 to restore the caller's banking state, and returns.
Assumptions: This entry is reached only from the empty/no-projectile slot path with one outstanding DEC $01.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, $0218,X, $01, and return-address stack bytes; X and Y are preserved.
Hardware changes: Restores CPU-port $01 banking by one increment; no VIC-II/CIA/SID register write.

Purpose: consume and prepare the next component of a composite sprite definition. Inputs: $02/$03 definition pointer, Y record cursor, and X slot. Purpose: decode a compressed 63-byte sprite and place its part. Inputs: X slot, Y record cursor, and valid compressed-stream context. Outputs: decoded cache and configured part slot are produced. Purpose: place an already decoded sprite part into the selected composite slot. Inputs: A is preserved across setup, $C5/$C6 hold saved X/Y, and ($02),Y addresses the part record. Purpose: merge a sprite part into its composite destination under the current mask mode. Inputs: decoded source, destination pointer, placement and flip state, and mode $F1. Purpose: select the backing buffer for a sprite slot. Inputs: X is sprite-slot index and slot flags are valid. Outputs: the destination pointer is installed in compositor zero page. Purpose: merge the cached decoded sprite mask into the active destination. Inputs: $02C0 cache, destination pointer, three masks, and mode $F1. Purpose: resolve and expand one tokenized sprite into the fixed 63-byte decode buffer, unless the alternate $C7 mode suppresses decoding
Inputs: A = sprite index; mode byte $C7; split source-pointer tables $C68C/$C78C plus base $068C; token stream at resolved $06/$07
Outputs: normal mode fills exactly $02C0-$02FE and returns A=$FF, X=$3F; tokens $69-$6F emit zero runs and $68 escapes a literal; alternate $C7 bit-6 mode adjusts pointer state and returns A=0 without filling the buffer
Assumptions: the sprite index resolves to a valid terminated/length-bounded token stream
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, source pointer $06/$07, and decoder scratch
Hardware changes: none; writes only the 63-byte RAM sprite buffer

Expand a packed sprite into the 63-byte cache $02C0-$02FE from pointer $06/$07. Bytes $69-$6F emit 1-7 zeros; $68 escapes the following byte as one literal, including reserved values. Other bytes are literals. X counts output bytes; Y counts input bytes; return A=$FF. Every one of the 162 main-pool records expands to exactly 63 bytes and consumes precisely the distance to the next record.

Purpose: Resolve The Basement playable phase's alternate raw sprite pointer without decoding the 63-byte cache.

Assumptions: The encoded selector maps to a valid raw sprite address in the active phase occupant.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, Z, C, and $06/$07; X and the 63-byte cache are preserved.

25-byte instruction continuation of $B83F, including undocumented LAX absolute,Y at $B852. LAX loads both A/X from the $DC36+Y I/O address; SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4 select paths that execute optional BIT instructions. Four native combinations of comparison operands/carry passed, and LAX A/X matched the stopped CIA timer value for Y=0. The comparisons change the path, not the stored value; exact raster timing and purpose of the comparisons remain open.
